frontier_action_performed: Pursued the highest-priority unresolved component-attribution questions for MARS and GEA using their primary PDFs; MARS Figure 3 was visually inspected, and the GEA paper was searched for explicit ablations/no-sharing variants.

evidence: Figure 3a visually shows final Lite Any Medal Rate around 0.74 for full MARS versus about 0.62 without Modular Decomposition.

Figure 3b visually shows full Comparative Reflective Memory around 0.75, a non-comparative/only-reflective memory variant around 0.62, and no memory around 0.52 at the 24-hour endpoint. These are graph-read approximate values, not table-extracted exact numbers.
Figure 3c visually shows Budget-Aware MCTS around 0.74, Vanilla MCTS around 0.64, and Greedy Search around 0.59 at 24 hours, again approximate graph readings.
The paper separately reports effective-solution rate 19.5% +/- 1.5% for Budget-Aware MCTS versus 16.1% +/- 1.3% for Vanilla MCTS.
Lesson utilization is 65.8% +/- 1.1% and cross-branch lesson transfer is 63.0% +/- 1.8%.
A causal-accuracy audit over 3,611 distilled solution lessons judged 88.34% correctly attributed metric shifts to code changes; manual inspection of 20 lessons yielded 90% causal accuracy.
Cost-controlled comparison: a 4-hour MARS run achieved 28.4% Any Medal at $9.6, versus the cited 24-hour AIRA-dojo baseline 24.4% at $39.0; full 24-hour MARS cost $60.5 and achieved 43.1%.
new_evidence.judgment: MARS component causality is now materially stronger than in the prior checkpoint: modularity, any-memory, comparative-delta memory, and budget-aware search each have directional isolated ablations. Exact endpoint values from Figure 3 remain approximate unless recovered from underlying logs/data. Cross-branch transfer remains an active-use statistic, not an isolated causal ablation.

evidence: The primary method explicitly couples two changes: Performance-Novelty parent-group selection and group-level experience aggregation/sharing.
The DGM-style comparator is single-parent tree evolution with branches isolated and no cross-branch sharing; the paper reports comparable evolved-agent counts.
Full-text search found no section labeled ablation and no explicit no-sharing variant in the current v1 paper.
new_evidence.judgment: GEA remains strong composite evidence that group-centric evolution works better under the tested coding setup, but it does not identify whether the uplift is caused primarily by group selection, pooled experience, or their interaction. Do not attribute the 71.0 vs 56.7 / 88.3 vs 68.3 gaps to experience sharing alone.
